chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) used to ask Shihab to give from his Zakat for his mawali (clients/slaves), and indeed, the Zakat was prohibited upon them (the Imams), but not upon their mawali.
ai.seo_question: Are the mawali of the Imams eligible to receive Zakat?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between the Imams' personal exemption from Zakat and the eligibility of their mawali (clients/freed slaves) to receive it, illustrating the practical application of the Prophet's lineage privilege. It highlights the Imam's active role in ensuring his dependents receive their rightful share, reinforcing the concept that while the Ahl al-Bayt are excluded from Zakat, their broader community and clients remain eligible recipients.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> used to ask Shihaab (to give) his<sup>asws</sup> Zakat to his<sup>asws</sup> slaves, and rather the Zakat is Probibited unto them<sup>asws</sup> but (it is permissible for our<sup>asws</sup>) slaves’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from Tha’labah ibn Maymun who has said the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would ask Shihab (ibn ‘Abd Rabbihi) to pay zakat due from him to his (Imam’s) servants. It is not permissible for them (’A’immah) to receive zakat, but it is permissible for their servants.”
